Three sources, one set of answers.

Where it does not, the differences are listed under each brand, and pages 3 to 5 ask for your pick on each one so the website, print, and signage all follow the same rule.

Colors were measured from the script word in each file, on white. Live-site files were pulled September 19 from mysymbios.com and its four practice sites. Guide artwork is from pages 8 to 11 of the brand guide. The approved zip files are 2000 pixels wide, the largest copies anyone has; the live site serves 345 to 430 pixel versions.

Your picks

Nine decisions. Check one per item and send it back.

1

Green and cyan values

Every PrimaryCare logo uses green #4ea647 and every Aria logo uses cyan #1bbed5: on the live site, in the guide artwork, and in the zip. The guide's swatch page prints different numbers (#4fa317 and #08bed5). One set has to be the reference for the website, print, and signage.

Use the logo artwork values (#4ea647, #1bbed5) and correct the swatch page
Use the swatch page values and have the logos recolored to match

Our recommendation: the artwork values. They are what every patient has already seen.

Notes
2

Header lockup: tagline or no tagline

The zip drops the tagline from Health, PrimaryCare, PhysioTherapy, and Fit. The live site, the guide's logo pages, and your email signature all use the single-line version with "Healthy, fit and beautiful for life."

Website headers keep the tagline version; the bare version is for small uses and signage
Website headers switch to the bare version from the zip
Something else (note below)

Our recommendation: keep the tagline in web headers. It reads at that size and it is what the campus has used for years.

Notes
3

SymbiosHealth: single line or stacked

The zip's SymbiosHealth is the stacked version with "Health" dropped below "Symbios." Everything else uses the single line.

Single line (current site, guide, signature)
Stacked (zip)
Both, with a rule for when each is used

Our recommendation: single line for headers and letterhead; stacked only where width is tight, such as social avatars.

Notes

Your picks, continued
4

Tagline size and alignment

The tagline is not built the same way across the lockups. On Health, PrimaryCare, and Aria it is right-aligned to the logo's edge; on PhysioTherapy it is centered under "Physio" and stops at three-quarters of the width. It is also set larger on Health than on Aria. At signage size those differences show.

Standardize: right-aligned to the logo edge, one size ratio, on all four
Leave as is

Our recommendation: standardize when the vector files are rebuilt. PrimaryCare is the cleanest reference.

Notes
5

SymbiosCare and SymbiosAlign taglines

Neither has a tagline in any source. The other lockups carry the campus line, and these two will sit next to them on the website and in print.

Use the campus tagline, "Healthy, fit and beautiful for life"
Use a "by Symbios Health" sub-line, as on some PrimaryCare and PhysioTherapy versions
No tagline; they stay clean
Write program-specific lines (note below)

Our recommendation: the campus tagline for consistency, unless you want Align and Care to read as programs rather than practices, in which case "by Symbios Health" fits.

Notes
6

Do Align and Care belong on the website?

Both have finished logos and neither has a page on the live site or the rebuild. Align is fully booked and your highest-value program; Care is the membership that ties the campus together. Patients hear both names from staff and will look for them.

Yes, a page for each in the campus navigation
Yes, but one page covering membership and programs together
Mention only, no dedicated pages yet
Not yet

Our recommendation: a page for each. A booked program still needs a page for referrals and the waitlist, and Care is the front door to everything else.

Notes

SymbiosEdge on the live site

theedge.mysymbios.com still serves the SymbiosEdge logo and title. The guide and the zip retire Edge in favor of SymbiosFit.

Fit everywhere; the rebuilt site already does this
Keep Edge somewhere (note below)

8

The H tail on SymbiosHealth

In every version, the tail of the H in "Health" drops through the tagline. It is in the original artwork.

Fix it in the vector file
Leave it; it is part of the mark

Our recommendation: fix it in the vector file. It is a two-minute change for whoever holds the source.

Notes
9

Vector masters

Nothing supplied so far is vector. The 2000 pixel zip files cover cards, letterhead, and the website. Anything over about six inches, including signage, needs Illustrator or EPS originals.

Darla or her designer supplies AI, EPS, or SVG for all seven lockups, in color, black, and white
Quantum Core redraws them as vectors from the zip files
Not needed right now

Our recommendation: ask for the originals first; if they do not exist, we redraw.
